subject: MATH
title: Geometry
description: A full-year high school Geometry course following the CA Common Core traditional pathway. Students build geometry from transformations, write two-column, paragraph and coordinate proofs, and apply congruence, similarity, right-triangle trigonometry, circles, area and volume to real modeling problems. The course closes with the CA Geometry conditional probability standards. Compass, straightedge, patty paper and free dynamic geometry software (GeoGebra) are used throughout.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics (Geometry); 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.G-CO.1: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment.
standards.G-CO.2: Represent transformations in the plane; describe transformations as functions of points.
standards.G-CO.3: Describe the rotations and reflections that carry a polygon onto itself.
standards.G-CO.4: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations.
standards.G-CO.5: Draw a transformed figure and specify a sequence of transformations that maps one figure onto another.
standards.G-CO.6: Use rigid motions to predict effects on figures and decide if two figures are congruent.
standards.G-CO.7: Use rigid motions to show two triangles are congruent iff corresponding parts are congruent.
standards.G-CO.8: Explain ASA, SAS, and SSS congruence criteria from rigid motions.
standards.G-CO.9: Prove theorems about lines and angles.
standards.G-CO.12: Make formal geometric constructions with compass and straightedge and other tools.
standards.G-CO.13: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.
standards.G-SRT.1: Verify properties of dilations given by a center and scale factor.
standards.G-SRT.2: Use similarity transformations to decide if two figures are similar.
standards.G-SRT.3: Use similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion.
standards.G-SRT.4: Prove theorems about triangles using similarity (triangle proportionality, Pythagorean theorem).
standards.G-SRT.5: Use congruence and similarity criteria to solve problems and prove relationships.
standards.G-SRT.6: Understand that trigonometric ratios are properties of angles in right triangles via similarity.
standards.G-SRT.7: Explain and use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles.
standards.G-SRT.8: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.
standards.G-SRT.9: (+) Derive the formula A = ½ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle.
standards.G-SRT.10: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.
standards.G-SRT.11: (+) Apply the Laws of Sines and Cosines to find unknown measures in triangles.
standards.G-C.1: Prove that all circles are similar.
standards.G-C.2: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords.
standards.G-C.3: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle; prove properties of angles of an inscribed quadrilateral.
standards.G-C.5: Derive arc length using similarity; define radian measure; derive the area of a sector.
standards.G-GPE.1: Derive the equation of a circle by completing the square.
standards.G-GPE.2: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.
standards.G-GPE.4: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
standards.G-GPE.5: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them.
standards.G-GPE.6: Find the point on a segment that partitions it in a given ratio.
standards.G-GPE.7: Use coordinates to compute perimeters and areas of polygons.
standards.G-GMD.1: Give informal arguments for circumference, area of circle, volume of cylinder, pyramid, cone formulas.
standards.G-GMD.3: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.
standards.G-GMD.4: Identify cross-sections of 3-D objects and 3-D objects generated by rotations.
standards.G-GMD.5: (CA) Know that the effect of a scale factor k > 0 on length, area, and volume is to multiply each by k, k², and k³.
standards.G-MG.1: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and properties to describe objects.
standards.G-MG.2: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations.
standards.G-MG.3: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems.
standards.S-CP.1: Describe events as subsets of a sample space using unions, intersections, complements.
standards.S-CP.2: Understand independence: P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).
standards.S-CP.4: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables.
standards.S-CP.5: Recognize and explain conditional probability and independence in everyday situations.
standards.S-CP.6: Find conditional probability as a fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A.
standards.S-CP.7: Apply the Addition Rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B).
standards.S-CP.9: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities.
standards.S-MD.6: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions.
standards.S-MD.7: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts.

units.title: Foundations and Constructions
units.big_idea: Geometry is built from precise definitions and tools.

units.title: Transformations and Rigid Motion
units.big_idea: Congruence means one figure maps onto another by rigid motions.

units.title: Congruence and Proof
units.big_idea: Logical arguments justify why geometric relationships always hold.

units.title: Quadrilaterals and Coordinate Proof
units.big_idea: Algebra on the coordinate plane can prove geometric theorems.

units.title: Similarity
units.big_idea: Dilations create proportional figures that preserve angles.

units.title: Right Triangles and Trigonometry
units.big_idea: Similar right triangles give fixed side ratios for each angle.

units.title: Circles
units.big_idea: All circles are similar; angles, arcs and chords relate in predictable ways.

units.title: Area, Volume and Modeling
units.big_idea: Formulas for measurement can be derived and applied to design.

units.title: Conditional Probability
units.big_idea: Probability quantifies uncertainty and depends on given information.

units.title: Course Review and Final
units.big_idea: Geometry ideas connect across transformations, proof and measurement.

weeks.topic: Points, lines, planes and precise definitions
objectives: Use undefined terms to define geometric figures

days.title: Undefined terms
days.work: Sketch and label points, lines and planes, then write definitions of segment, ray and angle using only undefined terms.

days.title: Segment measure
days.work: Use the Segment Addition Postulate and the distance on a number line to solve 10 problems like AB + BC = AC with algebra.

days.title: Angles
days.work: Measure and classify angles with a protractor and solve angle-addition problems with expressions like (3x + 5)°.

days.title: Angle pairs
days.work: Find complementary, supplementary, vertical and linear-pair angles in diagrams and write equations to find unknowns.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Quiz on definitions, segment and angle addition, and angle pairs.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on vocabulary and angle relationships.

days.title: Copy segment & angle
days.work: Construct a copy of a segment and an angle with compass and straightedge, writing the steps.

days.title: Bisectors
days.work: Construct a perpendicular bisector and an angle bisector, then verify by folding patty paper.

days.title: Perpendiculars & parallels
days.work: Construct a perpendicular through a point and a parallel line through a point not on a line.

days.title: GeoGebra constructions
days.work: Recreate all four constructions in GeoGebra and drag points to confirm they hold.

days.title: Construction check
days.work: Perform three constructions from memory and explain why each works using circle radii.

days.title: Midpoint formula
days.work: Derive and apply the midpoint formula, including finding an endpoint given a midpoint.

days.title: Distance formula
days.work: Derive the distance formula from the Pythagorean theorem and compute perimeters of polygons on the grid.

days.title: Partitioning
days.work: Find the point that divides a segment in ratios like 2:3 using the coordinate method.

days.title: Inscribed polygons
days.work: Construct an equilateral triangle, square and regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Unit 1 test: definitions, constructions, midpoint and distance.

objectives: Define and perform translations and reflections

days.title: Transformations as functions
days.work: Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle with those that don't (stretch) on a grid.

days.title: Translations
days.work: Translate polygons using rules like (x, y) → (x + 3, y – 5) and vector notation.

days.title: Reflections
days.work: Reflect figures over the axes, y = x and y = –x, and write coordinate rules.

days.title: Reflection definition
days.work: Use patty paper to show the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector of segments joining corresponding points.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on translation and reflection rules.

days.title: Rotations about origin
days.work: Rotate figures 90°, 180°, 270° about the origin and derive the coordinate rules.

days.title: Rotations about a point
days.work: Rotate a triangle about a point that isn't the origin with protractor and compass.

days.title: Symmetry
days.work: Find all lines of symmetry and rotation angles for regular polygons, rectangles and rhombi.

days.title: Real-world symmetry
days.work: Photograph three objects at home with symmetry (hubcap, tile, logo) and describe each symmetry.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on rotation rules and symmetry.

days.title: Compositions
days.work: Perform a translation followed by a reflection and compare to reversing the order.

days.title: Two reflections
days.work: Show reflecting over two parallel lines is a translation and over intersecting lines is a rotation.

days.title: Find the sequence
days.work: Given a figure and its image, write a sequence of rigid motions mapping one onto the other (8 problems).

days.title: Tessellation project
days.work: Design a translation or rotation tessellation on paper using a modified square.

days.title: Check
days.work: Short quiz plus tessellation explanation.

days.title: Congruence definition
days.work: Decide whether pairs of figures are congruent by finding a rigid motion or showing none exists.

days.title: Corresponding parts
days.work: Write congruence statements and list all corresponding congruent parts (CPCTC).

days.title: Triangle criteria
days.work: Build triangles from given sides/angles with straws to test SSS, SAS, ASA, SSA and AAA.

days.title: Explain criteria
days.work: Write a rigid-motion explanation of why SAS guarantees congruence.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Unit 2 test on transformations and congruence.

days.title: Inductive vs. deductive
days.work: Make conjectures from patterns and find counterexamples.

days.title: Conditionals
days.work: Rewrite statements in if-then form and write converse, inverse and contrapositive with truth values.

days.title: Laws of logic
days.work: Apply the Law of Detachment and Syllogism to draw valid conclusions.

days.title: Algebraic proof
days.work: Write two-column proofs solving equations with properties of equality.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on logic and algebraic proof.

weeks.topic: Proving theorems about lines and angles

days.title: Vertical angles proof

days.title: Transversals
days.work: Explore angle pairs formed by parallel lines and a transversal in GeoGebra and record conjectures.

days.title: Parallel line proofs
days.work: Prove alternate interior angles congruent from the corresponding angles postulate.

days.title: Converses
days.work: Use converses to prove lines parallel and solve algebraic angle problems.

days.title: Proof quiz
days.work: Write two proofs independently for a quiz.

objectives: Prove the triangle angle sum theorem

days.title: Angle sum
days.work: Prove that triangle angles sum to 180° using a parallel line, and apply the Exterior Angle Theorem.

days.title: Isosceles triangles
days.work: Prove the base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent using a reflection or SAS.

days.title: Midsegment
days.work: Explore and prove the midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long (coordinate proof).

days.title: Concurrency
days.work: Construct medians, angle bisectors and perpendicular bisectors and locate centroid, incenter and circumcenter.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on triangle theorems.

objectives: Write congruence proofs using SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL

days.title: SSS & SAS proofs
days.work: Write four two-column proofs using SSS and SAS.

days.title: ASA, AAS, HL
days.work: Write proofs with ASA, AAS and HL and identify when SSA fails.

days.title: CPCTC
days.work: Prove triangles congruent and then use CPCTC to prove segments or angles congruent.

days.title: Overlapping triangles
days.work: Separate overlapping triangles by redrawing and complete two proofs.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Unit 3 test: logic, line/angle proofs and triangle congruence proofs.

objectives: Prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram

days.title: Polygon angle sums
days.work: Derive the interior angle sum (n – 2)·180° and find interior/exterior angles of regular polygons.

days.title: Parallelogram properties
days.work: Prove opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent using a diagonal and ASA.

days.title: Diagonals
days.work: Prove diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

days.title: Proving parallelograms
days.work: Use the five tests to decide if a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on parallelogram properties.

weeks.topic: Rectangles, rhombi, squares, trapezoids and kites

days.title: Rectangles
days.work: Prove diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and use it to solve problems.

days.title: Rhombi & squares
days.work: Prove diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular and bisect angles.

days.title: Trapezoids & kites
days.work: Explore trapezoid midsegment and kite diagonal properties in GeoGebra.

days.title: Quadrilateral hierarchy
days.work: Build a Venn diagram/hierarchy of quadrilaterals and justify placements.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on special quadrilaterals.

days.title: Slope criteria
days.work: Show parallel lines have equal slopes and perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals using rotation.

days.title: Writing lines
days.work: Write equations of lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line through a point.

days.title: Classify by coordinates
days.work: Prove a quadrilateral with given vertices is a rectangle, rhombus or square.

days.title: Area on the plane
days.work: Compute the area of polygons on the plane with decomposition.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Unit 4 test on quadrilaterals and coordinate proof.

days.title: Dilation by construction
days.work: Dilate a triangle from a center with scale factors 2 and 1/2 using a ruler.

days.title: Properties
days.work: Verify that a dilation maps a line not through the center to a parallel line and scales lengths by k.

days.title: Coordinate dilations
days.work: Dilate figures about the origin and other points with the rule (x, y) → (kx, ky).

days.title: Similarity transformations
days.work: Find a sequence of rigid motions plus dilation mapping one figure to another.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on dilations.

objectives: Solve problems with SAS~ and SSS~

days.title: AA criterion
days.work: Use dilations to explain why two pairs of congruent angles give similar triangles.

days.title: SSS~ and SAS~
days.work: Decide which triangles are similar and write similarity statements.

days.title: Indirect measurement lab
days.work: Measure a tree's height with the mirror method and with shadows; compare results.

days.title: Similarity proofs
days.work: Write two similarity proofs.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on similarity criteria.

objectives: Prove the Pythagorean theorem using similarity

days.title: Side splitter
days.work: Prove a line parallel to one side divides the other sides proportionally.

days.title: Angle bisector theorem
days.work: Apply the angle bisector theorem to find segment lengths.

days.title: Altitude to hypotenuse
days.work: Show the altitude to the hypotenuse creates three similar triangles and find geometric means.

days.title: Pythagorean proof
days.work: Prove the Pythagorean theorem from similar triangles; compare to a dissection proof.

days.title: Scale factor effects
days.work: Investigate how scale factor k changes perimeter, area (k²) and volume (k³) using cubes.

days.title: Review transformations
days.work: Mixed review of transformations and congruence problems.

days.title: Review proof
days.work: Practice four proofs from Units 3–4.

days.title: Review similarity
days.work: Mixed similarity problems including indirect measurement.

days.title: Semester exam
days.work: Take the semester exam.

days.title: Error analysis
days.work: Correct exam errors and write explanations for each mistake.

weeks.topic: Pythagorean theorem and special right triangles

days.work: Solve applied problems (ladders, TV diagonals) with the Pythagorean theorem.

days.title: Converse
days.work: Use the converse and inequalities to classify triangles as acute, right or obtuse.
Derive 45-45-90 ratios from a square's diagonal and solve problems.
Derive 30-60-90 ratios from an equilateral triangle and solve problems.

days.work: Quiz on Pythagorean theorem and special right triangles.

objectives: Define sine, cosine, tangent through similarity

objectives: Derive area formula ½ab sin C
